args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. Deployment history shows v2.3.1 and v2.3.1-rc were both unhealthy. I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent healthy release, in all regions; the rollback completed and was verified in us-east, us-west and eu-west. Next steps: confirm health and error rate have recovered, and find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, was failing health checks and had an 18% error rate. The release candidate before it, v2.3.1-rc, was also marked unhealthy.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release marked healthy. The deployment list isn't in time order, so I went by its sequence numbers to find the latest one. The rollback finished in all three regions.
- **Now:** checkout-api is healthy on v2.3.0 everywhere, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the next steps: keep watching health and find out what broke in v2.3.1 before deploying it again. I wrote it before the post-rollback status check came back, so it says recovery still needs confirming. The service has since recovered, which you may want to add to the incident.

content.text: The list isn't fully in seq order, but going by seq, v2.3.0 (seq 1) is the newest healthy release. The two releases after it (v2.3.1-rc at seq 2 and v2.3.1 at seq 3) are both unhealthy.
